components.name: JinshuDiff
components.summary: What changed between two versions of a Jinshu document, block by block, with words struck and inserted
components.description: JinshuDiff compares two versions of a document and shows what changed: blocks added, removed, moved and modified, each in a card tinted by its kind, with the unchanged runs between them folded. A summary counts each kind and steps between the changes. A modified block shows its words struck and inserted in place, or the whole block before and after when the edit is too heavy to read word by word; `mode` chooses.

props.description: A diff computed in Logic with `diffDocuments`, in place of `a` and `b`; for a long document.

props.name: mode
props.description: `smart` shows words for a light edit and the whole block for a heavy one; `inline` always words; `block` always whole blocks.

notes: Each card names its kind in words (added, removed, moved, changed), so the tint is never the only sign.
Removed words are struck through as well as tinted; the before and after sides of a heavy edit are labelled.
The stepper's buttons are named Previous and Next, and the position is read beside them.

components.name: JinshuEditor
components.summary: A Jinshu document, edited block by block, with history, saving, and a review of what an agent changed or asks
components.description: JinshuEditor edits a Jinshu document where it is read: each block keeps the reader's geometry, so moving between reading and editing does not jump. Text blocks edit in place; tables, code, folds, callouts, columns and media have their own editors, and `/` inserts any block. On a live `channel` the source keeps the history, the save state and the review: an agent's change is marked at each block it touched, with a bar to view or undo that batch; its suggestions and save requests wait in one queue; and an agent at work shows a mark the person can stop. Pasted paragraphs or Markdown become blocks, and in a Markdown document (`format`) the menus offer only what Markdown holds. Source mode edits the whole document as Markdown text and applies only the changed blocks, in one undo step.

components.name: JinshuOutline
components.summary: A Jinshu document's headings as a contents list that moves the reader and shows each section's progress
components.description: JinshuOutline lists a document's headings, indented by level, as a contents list. Shared with a JinshuView or JinshuEditor through `useJinshuNav()`, pressing a heading scrolls the document to it and tints that heading as the one being read; with `nav.onVisibleChange` on the scroll holding a JinshuView, the tint follows the reader's scrolling too. An app can mark each section done, current or locked, as a course does.

components.name: JinshuView
components.summary: A Jinshu document, read: text, media, tables and the app's own blocks, with resume and reading observations
components.description: JinshuView draws a Jinshu document for reading: headings, paragraphs, lists, callouts, folds, code, formulas, tables, images, video, audio, files and the app's own `x-` blocks. It reads a document the page holds (`doc`), or follows a live one that Logic serves (`channel` and `docKey`), so an edit made elsewhere, by a person or an agent, appears as it lands. It can offer to continue where the reader stopped, open at one block, hold media to a policy, and report what was read and played through `onObserve`.

props.name: doc
props.description: The document, held by the page: `null` says it is unavailable, `undefined` that it is still loading. Leave it out to read a live `channel`.

props.name: channel
props.description: The page's `syncDoc` action, which Logic answers with `source.serve`: the reader follows the live document.

props.name: docKey
props.description: Which document `channel` serves.

props.name: nav
props.description: From `useJinshuNav()`, shared with a `JinshuOutline`: pressing a heading scrolls the reader to it. Give `nav.onVisibleChange` to the `<scroll>` holding the reader to follow the heading being read and report dwell and position.

props.name: resume
props.description: Saved progress: offers to continue at its position and resumes media where it stopped.

props.name: openAt
props.description: A top-level block to open at, once: where an agent's change landed (a tool result's `page`).

props.name: onObserve
props.description: What was read and played, in batches: played media ranges and events from custom blocks; dwell per block and the reading position once `nav` hears the scroll. Facts only; the app decides what counts as done.

props.name: filePolicy
props.description: Whether files may show inline or only as attachments.

props.name: mediaPolicy
props.description: How media may be scrubbed (`any`, `played-only`, `none`) and the fastest rate offered.

props.name: resolveSrc
props.description: Turns a block's `src` into what the page loads: a signed URL, a custom scheme.

props.name: customBlocks
props.description: Renderers for the app's own block types, keyed by `x-scope-name`.

props.name: customInlines
props.description: Renderers for the app's own inline atoms, keyed by `x-scope-name`.

notes: The title and each heading are headings at their level, so a screen reader can move between sections.
Lists are lists of items; a task's box is a checkable item named by its text.
Images are named by `alt`, then the caption; a formula is named by its LaTeX; media controls are named by the block's title or caption.
Selection is budgeted per page: past the budget, further text renders unselectable rather than slowing the page.

gaps.today: The header row scrolls with the table; it stays aligned with its columns as the table scrolls sideways.

limits: The reader shows no change bar or review queue; an agent's changes appear in place, briefly tinted with `hasUpdateHighlights`. Changes made while no editor was open wait for the next `JinshuEditor`.
`openAt` brings the block to the nearest edge of the scroll, not to its top.

Dwell is measured per top-level block from scrolling alone: time with the page hidden or the reader away shows as one long `idleMs` stretch, and time since the last scroll is not reported when the page closes.
Every block is mounted; the page's scroll belongs to the app, so the reader does not mount blocks by viewport.
It has no AI entry of its own: an agent reaches documents only through the tools the app registers with `createJinshuTools`.
